**Option (A):** $2\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=n+1-i}^n f(i/n,j/n)\frac{1}{n^2}$.

By symmetry $f(x,y)=f(y,x)$, the integral over the lower triangle $\{x+y\le 1\}$ equals the integral over the upper triangle $\{x+y\ge 1\}$. Each triangle has integral $\frac12\iint_D f$. The sum in (A) is a Riemann sum over the upper triangle, tending to $\frac12\iint_D f$. Multiplying by 2 gives $\iint_D f$. ✓
